citations.quote: the VaR of a portfolio with loss L at the confidence level α is given by the smallest number l such that the probability that the loss L exceeds l is no larger than 1 − α.
The 95% VaR value is approximately 2.2, indicating that there is a 5% chance that we lose at least this amount.
This result is routinely used in the variance–covariance approach (also known as the delta-normal approach) to computing risk measures.
